title: Observe explicit subject identities and content coherently
statement: The Work record storage Module shall inspect only explicitly supplied safe subject paths and return identities and requested content from the same observed bytes, with explicit absence or failure and no partial subject set when observed change prevents coherence.

what.problem: An identity derived from different bytes than the supplied content, or an automatically selected subject, misstates the basis an actor actually inspected.
what.desired_outcome: The actor can explicitly carry the inspected byte identity or expected absence into a later request without a hidden substitution.

why.rationale: SR-041 requires exact subject observations; MOD-011 owns the safe byte-observation boundary reused by publication freshness checks.

stakeholders: Engineers and agents supplying explicit command requests
Maintainers of MOD-011 and its Interface consumers

conditions: A caller requests identities for explicit contained engineering subjects, optionally with complete content.

contexts: IF-003 subject observation for the explicitly selected repository root and paths, presented through IF-004.

how.approach: Apply the published path and size/count rules, compute identities from the same inspected bytes, and preserve absence and observed-change outcomes without executing or interpreting subject content as instructions.

how_much.scope: Explicit subject paths and admitted identity-only or full-content modes; no dependency discovery, inferred workflow subjects, or universal Git requirement.

acceptance_criteria: Every returned identity names its explicit path and derives from the same bytes supplied when full content is requested; complete output is not silently truncated.

A missing subject is represented as explicit expected absence rather than a fabricated non-null stored Subject; a nonregular, symlinked, unsafe, unreadable, or over-limit subject receives its applicable safe outcome.
An observed change that prevents coherent identity/content results produces conflict without a partial subject set, preserving the existing observed-check limitation for outside edits.

Only the declared paths are inspected; content is not executed, and no stage or record interpretation adds new subjects. Identity-only output does not claim that the actor reviewed sufficient content.

Observed identities are returned for the actor to supply explicitly later; this operation neither refreshes historical recorded subjects nor silently replaces the expected basis of a subsequent write.

sources.basis: Derive this draft lower-level obligation from the containing SR at the selected command or operational-record responsibility boundary. Allocation and acceptance criteria are design claims for review, not implementation, requirement approval, or satisfaction evidence.

Preserve the applicable current public and stored-record guarantees at this accountable boundary. The named source retains exact schemas, operation tables, classifications, limits, and historical adoption obligations; this allocation neither replaces those details nor accepts REM authoring JSON as operational records.
